agent-skill.passage: A skill's name is at most 64 characters of lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens, with no XML tags and neither reserved word, anthropic or claude; its description is non-empty, at most 1,024 characters, and holds no XML tags.

authority.decision: A repository counts as generated from CLAUDE.md only on the signals check 2 of references/audit-policy.md names, the layout of this source's retired init-ai-config generator, so a repository that keeps its instructions another way is never reported as drifted.

behavioral.passage: Give Claude a way to verify its work, such as tests, a linter, or an expected output, because it does markedly better when it can check its own results.

behavioral.decision: An agent's instructions forbid disabling, suppressing, or working around a failing check and state a quality gate, as this source's own CLAUDE.md does under Required validation.

claude-agent.passage: A project subagent is a Markdown file in .claude/agents whose frontmatter requires a name, of at most 256 characters without a colon, and a description, and whose tools, given as a comma-separated string or a YAML list, inherit every tool when omitted, beside optional model and hooks.

claude-hook.passage: A hook is configured under hooks, by event name, as matcher groups whose hooks list holds handlers of type command, http, mcp_tool, prompt, or agent, each with its required field, an optional timeout in seconds that defaults to 600 for command, http, and mcp_tool, and, on command and http hooks, onFailure of continue or block.
A settings file with an unknown hook event name fails only that entry, so its hooks never run.

claude-memory.passage: Target under 200 lines per CLAUDE.md file, since longer files consume more context and reduce adherence.

A CLAUDE.md imports a file with @path syntax outside code spans and fenced blocks, resolved relative to the importing file, and imports help organize a long file but don't reduce its context cost, because imported files also load at launch.
Every .md file under .claude/rules is discovered recursively; a rule is scoped to files by a paths frontmatter list of globs, and rules without a paths field are loaded unconditionally.

claude-settings.passage: The shared .claude/settings.json is committed for everyone working in the folder, while .claude/settings.local.json holds personal overrides for one project and stays out of git.

permissions.allow rules and permissions.additionalDirectories entries in a project's .claude/settings.json grant capability, so Claude Code applies them only after the workspace trust dialog is accepted.
permissions.defaultMode is one of default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions, or manual, and auto and bypassPermissions don't take effect from project or local settings.

claude-skill.passage: argument-hint is the hint shown during autocomplete to indicate expected arguments, and $ARGUMENTS holds all arguments passed when the skill is invoked.

claude-skill.decision: A Claude Code skill that reads $ARGUMENTS gives an argument-hint, so the person invoking it sees what to pass: check 8 of references/audit-policy.md.

codex-agent.passage: A project's custom agents are TOML files under .codex/agents that must define name, description, and developer_instructions, and sandbox_mode, approval_policy, model_provider, and mcp_servers in such a file don't override the parent configuration.

codex-hook.passage: Codex loads a trusted project's hooks from .codex/hooks.json or the [hooks] tables of .codex/config.toml, merging both with a warning, under the events PreToolUse, PermissionRequest, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, UserPromptSubmit, SubagentStop, Stop, Interrupt, SessionStart, SubagentStart, and SessionEnd, and a hook without a timeout runs up to 600 seconds, or 1 second on SessionEnd and Interrupt.

codex-rule.passage: Project rules under .codex/rules are Starlark prefix_rule calls whose non-empty pattern names a command prefix and whose decision, allow by default, is allow, prompt, or forbidden, where allow runs the command outside the sandbox without prompting; they load only when the project's .codex layer is trusted.

codex-skill.passage: Codex scans .agents/skills in a repository, and a skill's agents/openai.yaml sets policy.allow_implicit_invocation, true by default, to false so Codex does not invoke the skill implicitly from a prompt.

codex-skill.decision: A skill under .agents/skills that stands for one under .claude/skills carries its description, so every runtime chooses it on the same words: check 8 of references/audit-policy.md.

collision.decision: A skill or custom agent named code-review collides with Copilot's built-in agent, and an unmarked AGENTS.md or copilot-instructions.md is one the generator refuses to overwrite: checks 8 and 11 of references/audit-policy.md.

copilot-agent.passage: A custom agent is a .agent.md or .md file whose frontmatter requires a description, whose target is vscode or github-copilot, and whose tools list enables every tool when unset and none when empty.
Copilot CLI reads a repository's custom agents from .github/agents and personal ones from ~/.copilot/agents.

copilot-config.passage: A skill is a SKILL.md file that starts with YAML frontmatter.
A custom agent's profile starts with YAML frontmatter that sets its properties.

copilot-skill.passage: A skill's frontmatter gives a name, lowercase with hyphens and matching its folder, and a description of what it does and when to use it.
Copilot reads a repository's skills from folders under .github/skills, .claude/skills, and .agents/skills, each holding a SKILL.md.

inventory.passage: Claude Code reads CLAUDE.md from the project root, or from .claude/CLAUDE.md, at the start of every session.
A CLAUDE.local.md at the project root holds private per-project preferences that shouldn't be checked into version control, and markdown files in .claude/rules organize instructions by topic.
A project's shared Claude Code settings live in .claude/settings.json.
Codex reads AGENTS.override.md or AGENTS.md in each directory from the project root down to the working directory.

Each Copilot surface reads its own set of instruction files: .github/copilot-instructions.md, .github/instructions/*.instructions.md, and agent instructions such as AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and GEMINI.md.
Besides .codex/config.toml, a trusted project's .codex holds hooks.json, custom agents as TOML files under agents, and Starlark rules under rules.

layering.passage: In each directory from the project root down to the working directory, Codex takes the first non-empty file of AGENTS.override.md, AGENTS.md, and the names project_doc_fallback_filenames lists, and stops adding content at project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default.
project_doc_max_bytes sets the maximum number of bytes Codex reads from its AGENTS.md instruction files.

layering.decision: A root instruction file over project_doc_max_bytes is a WARNING rather than an ERROR, because a user's own Codex configuration may set another cap, which a static audit cannot read: check 7 of references/audit-policy.md.

layering.passage: Copilot CLI combines AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, and .github/copilot-instructions.md from the repository root, the working directory, and the directories between, and modular .github/instructions files from the same locations but not intermediate directories.

The instruction files Copilot Chat, the cloud agent, code review, and Copilot CLI read differ by surface and by editor: in VS Code, Copilot Chat reads AGENTS.md as its only agent file and code review reads only repository-wide instructions.

VS Code settings decide which instruction files its chat reads: chat.useAgentsMdFile for a root AGENTS.md, chat.useClaudeMdFile for CLAUDE.md, github.copilot.chat.codeGeneration.useInstructionFiles for .github/copilot-instructions.md, and chat.includeApplyingInstructions for applyTo instructions.

Copilot code review on GitHub reads a root AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, REVIEW.md, .github/copilot-instructions.md, and path-specific instructions, and skills in .github/skills, from the pull request's head branch.
Repository-wide instructions live in .github/copilot-instructions.md, and path-specific ones in .github/instructions/NAME.instructions.md, whose applyTo frontmatter names the files they cover.

limitation.decision: The audit names each documented limitation a repository hits rather than passing it silently: references/known-limitations.md.

mcp.passage: A project's shared MCP servers live in .mcp.json at the repository root, under mcpServers, each with a command for a stdio server or a url and a type of http, sse, or ws for a remote one. Claude Code reads an entry with no type as stdio, so it skips one with a url and no type, and it also skips a type sdk entry and a server with a reserved built-in name.
Codex reads MCP servers from mcp_servers tables in config.toml: a stdio server by its command, args, and env, and a streamable HTTP server by its url.

mcp.decision: The file shapes, the transport each target supports, and the precedence between .mcp.json and .github/mcp.json are this skill's record in check 6 of references/audit-policy.md.

orphan.decision: A shim whose canonical skill is gone, or a generated file the manifest no longer lists, carries stale instructions: check 5 of references/audit-policy.md and references/generated-layout.md.

ownership.decision: Every generated file carries the AUTO-GENERATED from CLAUDE.md marker or a manifest hash, so the generator never updates or deletes a file it does not own: check 10 of references/audit-policy.md.

parity.decision: Each generated file matches what the generator would write from CLAUDE.md, or its manifest hash: check 4 of references/audit-policy.md and references/generated-layout.md.

provenance.decision: A generated Copilot projection in .github/skills or .github/agents is one the manifest owns: check 8 of references/audit-policy.md.

runtime.passage: Custom instructions are enabled for Copilot code review by default, a repository setting on GitHub.com can disable them, and each user's personal choice of whether to use custom instructions must be enabled, as it is by default.

runtime.decision: Settings, policies, authentication, model availability, and enablement live outside the repository, so a static audit names them for checking by hand: check 7 of references/audit-policy.md.

runtime-role.decision: The manifest's runtimeRoles name each Copilot surface's role in the generated layout: check 8 of references/audit-policy.md and references/generated-layout.md.

scope.decision: The manifest is editable, so the scope it declares is compared with the literal targets of a recognized generator, read without running it: check 3 of references/audit-policy.md.

Without a manifest or a generator, the scope is the runtimes and surfaces the repository's own files show it serves, a CLAUDE.md for Claude Code, a root AGENTS.md, .codex, or .agents/skills for Codex, and a .github folder for Copilot's CLI, app, and code review, which read those files with no setting of the repository's own: check 3 of references/audit-policy.md.

scope.passage: Copilot CLI, the cloud agent, and code review on GitHub.com read agent instructions from AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or GEMINI.md, while Copilot Chat in JetBrains reads only .github/copilot-instructions.md and path-specific instructions.

trust-boundary.passage: Copilot code review on GitHub reads custom instructions, CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md, and REVIEW.md among them, and skills in .github/skills, from the pull request's head branch.

vocabulary.decision: Manifest runtimes, surfaces, and MCP targets use the canonical names of the generated layout: check 3 of references/audit-policy.md and references/generated-layout.md.
